cli.title: Claude Code
cli.tagline: Install the {{DISPLAY_NAME}} CLI and approve the connection in your browser.
steps: Install the {{CLI_BINARY}} CLI with pipx (get pipx at pipx.pypa.io).
Run the login command and approve the browser sign-in.
Ask Claude Code to use the {{CLI_BINARY}} command.
cli.verify: Run {{CLI_BINARY}} and confirm you are signed in.
cli.onboardHint: Paste this into Claude Code once the CLI is installed and signed in.

mcp.title: Claude Code
mcp.tagline: Add {{DISPLAY_NAME}} in your terminal, then sign in with OAuth.
steps: Run the command above in your terminal. --scope user makes {{DISPLAY_NAME}} available in every folder, not just the current one.
Start claude, run /mcp, select {{SERVER_ID}}, and choose Authenticate if it says Needs authentication.
Approve the {{DISPLAY_NAME}} sign-in in your browser and confirm {{SERVER_ID}} shows as connected.
mcp.verify: Open /mcp in Claude Code and confirm {{DISPLAY_NAME}} is connected.
mcp.onboardHint: Paste this into Claude Code once the MCP server is connected.

mcp.title: Claude Desktop
mcp.tagline: Add a custom connector in Claude — same flow for Claude Desktop, claude.ai, and Cowork. It also loads in Claude Code when you sign in with the same account.
steps: Open Claude Desktop, claude.ai, or Cowork and go to Customize → Connectors. On Team or Enterprise plans, an Owner must first add the connector in Organization settings → Connectors.
Click "+" → "Add custom connector". On Team or Enterprise, choose Custom → Web.
Paste {{MCP_URL}} as the Remote MCP Server URL, then click Add.
Click Connect on the new entry — not Configure. (If the card defaults to Configure, click "..." → Remove, then re-add. The first probe drives the OAuth flow.)
Approve the {{DISPLAY_NAME}} OAuth request. Anthropic brokers remote connector traffic from its cloud, even for Desktop and Cowork.
Enable the connector in a conversation from the "+" menu → Connectors before asking Claude to use {{DISPLAY_NAME}}.
mcp.verify: Ask Claude to use {{DISPLAY_NAME}}.
mcp.onboardHint: Paste this as your first message in Claude Desktop once it is connected.

mcp.title: ChatGPT Desktop
mcp.tagline: Add {{DISPLAY_NAME}} as an MCP server in the ChatGPT desktop app. No terminal needed.
steps: Open ChatGPT Desktop → Settings → MCP servers → Add server.
Choose Streamable HTTP as the transport. Name: {{SERVER_ID}}. URL: {{MCP_URL}}. Leave the authorization fields empty; the app signs you in on first use.
Save, then choose Restart when the app asks.
Approve the {{DISPLAY_NAME}} sign-in when it opens, then ask ChatGPT to use {{SERVER_ID}}.
Prefer the terminal? Pick Codex CLI in this menu; it shares this configuration (~/.codex).
mcp.verify: Type /mcp in the ChatGPT composer and confirm {{SERVER_ID}} is connected.
mcp.onboardHint: Paste this as your first message in ChatGPT Desktop once it is connected.

cli.title: Codex CLI
cli.tagline: Install the {{DISPLAY_NAME}} CLI and approve the connection in your browser.
steps: Install the {{CLI_BINARY}} CLI with pipx (get pipx at pipx.pypa.io).
Run the login command and approve the browser sign-in.
Ask Codex CLI to use the {{CLI_BINARY}} command.
cli.verify: Run {{CLI_BINARY}} and confirm you are signed in.
cli.onboardHint: Paste this into Codex CLI once the CLI is installed and signed in.

mcp.title: Codex CLI
mcp.tagline: Add {{DISPLAY_NAME}} as a Streamable HTTP MCP server in Codex, then run the OAuth login command.
mcp.command:
codex mcp add {{SERVER_ID}} --url {{MCP_URL}}
codex mcp login {{SERVER_ID}}
steps: Run the add command below in a terminal (skip it if the server is already listed).
Run the login command to start the browser OAuth flow.
Ask Codex to use the {{SERVER_ID}} MCP server.
mcp.verify: Run /mcp in the Codex TUI and confirm {{SERVER_ID}} is connected.
mcp.onboardHint: Paste this into Codex CLI once the MCP server is connected.

mcp.title: Cursor
mcp.tagline: Add {{DISPLAY_NAME}} to Cursor with one click, or through Cursor Settings.
steps: Click Add to Cursor above and confirm the new MCP server when Cursor asks.
Or add it by hand: Cursor Settings → Tools & MCP → New MCP server, then add the {{SERVER_ID}} entry shown below to mcp.json.
When {{SERVER_ID}} shows Needs login, click it and approve the {{DISPLAY_NAME}} sign-in in your browser.
Cursor Agent in the terminal reads the same mcp.json: run agent mcp login {{SERVER_ID}} there.
mcp.verify: Ask Cursor's agent to use {{DISPLAY_NAME}}.
mcp.onboardHint: Paste this as your first message in Cursor once it is connected.

cli.title: Antigravity
cli.tagline: Install the {{DISPLAY_NAME}} CLI and approve the connection in your browser.
steps: Install the {{CLI_BINARY}} CLI with pipx (get pipx at pipx.pypa.io).
Run the login command and approve the browser sign-in.
Ask Antigravity to use the {{CLI_BINARY}} command.
cli.verify: Run {{CLI_BINARY}} and confirm you are signed in.
cli.onboardHint: Paste this into Antigravity once the CLI is installed and signed in.

mcp.title: Antigravity
mcp.tagline: Add {{DISPLAY_NAME}} as a remote MCP server in Antigravity.
steps: Add the {{SERVER_ID}} entry shown above to the shared ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json file. In Antigravity IDE, open the agent panel, choose MCP Servers → Manage MCP Servers → View raw config; Antigravity CLI reads the same global file.
After the server appears, open Agent Settings (Cmd+, on macOS or Ctrl+, on Windows/Linux), select Customizations, and click Authenticate. Antigravity uses dynamic client registration (DCR) with PKCE.
Complete {{DISPLAY_NAME}} authorization in the browser and copy the authorization code.
Paste the authorization code into Antigravity and click Submit.
Wait for Antigravity to reconnect automatically, then confirm the server is connected.
mcp.verify: Ask Antigravity to use {{DISPLAY_NAME}}.
mcp.onboardHint: Paste this as your first message in Antigravity once it is connected.
mcp.caveat: Windows Antigravity 2.0/IDE remote OAuth remains unresolved after one QA failure. If the documented flow does not reconnect, use Product CLI and record Antigravity client logs plus server OAuth traces; do not add custom authentication fields.

mcp.title: Gemini CLI
mcp.tagline: Add {{DISPLAY_NAME}} to Gemini CLI in your terminal; Gemini discovers the OAuth sign-in on its own.
steps: Run the command above in your terminal.
Start gemini and run /mcp. Gemini CLI opens your browser to sign in to {{DISPLAY_NAME}} on first use.
Ask Gemini CLI to use {{SERVER_ID}}.
mcp.verify: Run /mcp in Gemini CLI and confirm {{SERVER_ID}} is connected.
mcp.onboardHint: Paste this into Gemini CLI once the MCP server is connected.

mcp.title: Goose
mcp.tagline: Add {{DISPLAY_NAME}} to Goose Desktop with one click, or from the Extensions screen.
steps: Click Add to Goose above and approve the extension when Goose asks. Goose opens your browser to sign in to {{DISPLAY_NAME}}.
Or add it by hand: open the Goose sidebar → Extensions → Add custom extension.
Type: Streamable HTTP. Endpoint URL: {{MCP_URL}}. ID: {{SERVER_ID}}. Name: {{DISPLAY_NAME}}. Leave the timeout at its default and click Add.
Approve the {{DISPLAY_NAME}} sign-in in the browser window Goose opens.
Using the goose CLI instead? Run goose configure → Add Extension → Remote Extension (Streamable HTTP) and answer the prompts with the same name and URL.
mcp.verify: Ask Goose to use {{DISPLAY_NAME}}.
mcp.onboardHint: Paste this as your first message in Goose once it is connected.

mcp.title: OpenCode
mcp.tagline: Add {{DISPLAY_NAME}} to OpenCode in your terminal, then sign in with OAuth.
mcp.command:
opencode mcp add {{SERVER_ID}} --url {{MCP_URL}}

Ask OpenCode to use {{SERVER_ID}}.
mcp.verify: Run opencode mcp list and confirm {{SERVER_ID}} is connected.
mcp.onboardHint: Paste this into OpenCode once the MCP server is connected.

mcp.title: Other MCP client
mcp.tagline: Any MCP-speaking client. Paste this URL and authorize.
steps: Add {{DISPLAY_NAME}} as a remote MCP server using streamable HTTP.
Paste {{MCP_URL}}.
Complete {{DISPLAY_NAME}} OAuth in the client. OAuth is product-owned.
mcp.verify: Confirm {{DISPLAY_NAME}} tools are available.
mcp.onboardHint: Paste this as your first message in Other MCP client once it is connected.
